terms.name: ALS Beamline 11.0.1.2
terms.definition: ALS Beamline 11.0.1.2, resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) with a reflectometer endstation. Source EPU5; photon energy 165–1,500 eV. ALS public range 165–1,500 eV. Blueprint beam note: ~200–1500 eV. Polarization is user selectable; linear polarization continuously variable from horizontal to vertical; left and right elliptical (or circular) polarization. Spot size = 100 μm diameter. Field of view/spatial resolution = down to 2 nm resolution. Sample information: Polymer thin films, solid thin films, vacuum compatible liquid cell. terms.name: Beam stop
terms.definition: §B.4 A small block on the camera body in front of the sensor . Hides the direct beam , which would saturate the sensor; because it rides on the camera, a CCD X move needs the opposite Beam Stop X move to keep the beam covered. Its motors are the SmarAct X and Y axes, only Y in use and parked until its encoders are shielded (Thomas, 2026-09-09). Next cycle it becomes a photodiode ( AI 6 ). Beam Stop X −4 … 19.5 mm · typ −1.7 Beam Stop Y −20 … 20 µm · typ 0 AI 6 BeamStop 100 nA/V

terms.name: Detector
terms.definition: §B.3 The 2D camera ( AXIS-SXR-40 , bare sCMOS sensor) on an arc, a sideways slide and an in/out slide; the plate on top of its face (the forehead ) is the part that collides. CCD Θ swings the whole camera up through the scattering angles (−6° stop: the PEEM pass-through pipe; +122° stop: the in-chamber slits); CCD X moves it sideways (growing toward the back wall) so the spot lands elsewhere on the sensor, or at 90 puts the door-side photodiode in the beam; CCD Y sets the distance, hence the angles that fit on the sensor. CCD Y is motor counts between two hard stops, not a distance ; presets BS Center / BS Edge put the beam stop at the sensor centre or its edge (Thomas, 2026-09-09). CCD Theta −6 … 122 ° · typ 0 CCD X −100 … 95 mm · typ −10.2 · 90 = Photodiode Far CCD Y 0 … 80.05 mm · typ parked 80 (safe)

terms.name: Ring lamp and video camera
terms.definition: §B.6 A ring light and a video camera outside the vacuum , looking through a viewport at the top of the chamber right above the in-chamber slits, in the beam direction (Thomas, 2026-09-09). The lamp lights the chamber so the camera can find the sample (YAG for the beam, crosshair for its position); it must be off during any exposure or the bare sensor records background and blobs. terms.name: Sample stage
terms.definition: §B.2 A four-axis manipulator hanging from the back wall at pipe height: X slides the whole stack along the door axis, Y and Z form a cross on the rotation stage Θ , the sample bar bolts on top. X brings the bar into the beam (out below 8 mm); Θ turns the bar from grazing (0°) to normal incidence (90°); Y and Z swap between along-the-beam and up/down as Θ turns. TEY is the drain current from the isolated sample plate. terms.definition: §A.13 Three sets (upstream, middle, in-chamber) of horizontal and vertical blade pairs ; JJ is the maker. Aperture moves a pair's two blades symmetrically to set the beam size, Trans moves both to set its position; aligned in order upstream → middle → in-chamber; hard limits, nothing can be damaged . All twelve read in mm (Thomas, 2026-09-09). 12 motors, no software limits · all read 0 on 2026-08-31 (encoders unplugged)

terms.name: Shutters
terms.definition: §A.12 A 2 ms fast shutter that times exposures, and one element downstream the old air shutter , kept as an emergency stop. They sit after the gold mesh, before the scatter slits (Thomas, 2026-09-09). The camera opens and closes the fast shutter around every exposure ; Shutter Inhibit (a software flag) stops it from opening, which is how a dark image is taken. fast 2 ms per cycle · air 100–120 ms, left open

class SimAI(StandardReadable):
    """A read-only analog input producing plausible values.

    The value stays within the engineering-unit range implied by the ADC
    voltage span and the ``Offset x Amplifier Sensitivity x Sensor Scale
    Factor`` chain. A background task (started on connect) applies a slowly
    drifting baseline plus Gaussian noise so live plots look alive.

    ``"Motor to AI"`` channels can instead be linked to a sim motor with
    `link_motor`, after which they track that motor's readback (with the
    configured noise) and the drift updater is disabled.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: AIConfig,
        update_period: float = DEFAULT_UPDATE_PERIOD,
        time_scale: float = 1.0,
        rng: random.Random | None = None,
        name: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self._update_period = update_period
        self._time_scale = time_scale
        self._rng = rng or random.Random()
        self._update_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self._linked_motor: SimLVMotor | None = None

        low, high = config.value_range
        span = high - low
        # Start the drifting baseline somewhere in the middle 60% of the range
        self._baseline = low + span * self._rng.uniform(0.2, 0.8)

        with self.add_children_as_readables(Format.HINTED_SIGNAL):
            self.value, self._set_value = soft_signal_r_and_setter(
                float, self._baseline, units=config.units
            )
        # The config-derived value range is NOT exposed as signals (real
        # hardware wouldn't have them); it bounds the drift/noise model in
        # `_tick` and is published as metadata via `devices.manifest()`.
        super().__init__(name=name)

    async def connect(
        self,
        mock: bool = False,
        timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
        force_reconnect: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        await super().connect(
            mock=mock, timeout=timeout, force_reconnect=force_reconnect
        )
        if self._update_task is None and self._linked_motor is None:
            self._update_task = asyncio.create_task(self._update_forever())

    def link_motor(self, motor: SimLVMotor) -> None:
        """Make this AI track ``motor``'s readback (Motor-to-AI channels)."""
        if self._update_task is not None:
            self._update_task.cancel()
            self._update_task = None
        self._linked_motor = motor
        motor.user_readback.subscribe_reading(self._on_motor_reading)

    def _on_motor_reading(self, readings: dict[str, Reading[float]]) -> None:
        (reading,) = readings.values()
        position = reading["value"]
        value = (
            (position - self.config.offset_v)
            * self.config.amp_sensitivity
            * self.config.scale_factor
        )
        if self.config.add_noise and self.config.noise_pct:
            value *= 1.0 + self._rng.gauss(0.0, self.config.noise_pct / 100.0)
        self._set_value(value)

    def seed_baseline(self, value: float) -> None:
        """Start the drift baseline at ``value`` (sim-config ``initial_state``).

        A pure initial condition: the random walk proceeds from here, it is
        not an anchor. Motor-linked AIs reject seeding — their value is the
        motor's position, so set the motor's initial position instead.

class SimBeamCurrent(SimAI):
    """The storage-ring beam current with a top-up sawtooth and drop control.

    The sawtooth shape and defaults (fill ~500, slow decay, top-up refill)
    are domain-knowledge assumptions, NOT from the config; correct them to
    the facility's real values via the constructor parameters. The one
    config-derived constraint: normal current stays above the "Beam Dumped"
    threshold (10) so that DIO reads False until the beam is deliberately
    dumped.

    Setting the sim-only ``sim_beam_on`` signal to False drops the current to
    ~0 quickly (flipping the derived "Beam Dumped" DIO); setting it back True
    refills slowly at ``recovery_rate`` — a beam dump is near-instantaneous
    but refilling the ring takes a while.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: AIConfig,
        update_period: float = DEFAULT_UPDATE_PERIOD,
        time_scale: float = 1.0,
        rng: random.Random | None = None,
        fill_current: float = 500.0,
        refill_threshold: float = 495.0,
        decay_rate: float = 0.2,
        recovery_rate: float = 5.0,
        dump_rate: float = 100.0,
        name: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        self._fill_current = fill_current
        self._refill_threshold = refill_threshold
        self._decay_rate = decay_rate
        self._recovery_rate = recovery_rate
        self._dump_rate = dump_rate
        # Sim-only control (will NOT exist on real hardware)
        self.sim_beam_on = soft_signal_rw(bool, True)
        self._beam_on = True
        self._beam_on_subscribed = False
        self._current = fill_current
        super().__init__(
            config,
            update_period=update_period,
            time_scale=time_scale,
            rng=rng,
            name=name,
        )
        self._set_value(self._current)

    @property
    def fill_current(self) -> float:
        """Nominal top-up fill current (the '100% beam' reference)."""
        return self._fill_current

    async def connect(
        self,
        mock: bool = False,
        timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
        force_reconnect: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        await super().connect(
            mock=mock, timeout=timeout, force_reconnect=force_reconnect
        )
        if not self._beam_on_subscribed:
            self.sim_beam_on.subscribe_reading(self._on_beam_on_changed)
            self._beam_on_subscribed = True

    def _on_beam_on_changed(self, readings: dict[str, Reading[bool]]) -> None:
        (reading,) = readings.values()
        self._beam_on = bool(reading["value"])

    def seed_baseline(self, value: float) -> None:
        """Start the sawtooth at ``value`` mA (sim-config ``initial_state``).

        The dynamics act immediately: below the refill threshold the top-up
        logic ramps back up (use ``sim_beam_on: false`` to keep it down).
        """
        if value < 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{self.config.label!r}: initial beam current must be >= 0, "
                f"got {value}"

    Camera-real controls (these exist as PVs on the actual IOC):

    - ``min_x`` / ``min_y`` / ``size_x`` / ``size_y``: ROI in binned pixels,
      aligned down (width x8, height/offsets x4) and clamped when a scan is
      prepared, exactly like the real driver's ``setROI()``.

      in *camera* time (``sim_time_scale`` only compresses wall time).

    Sim-only control (will not exist on the real IOC):

    - ``sim_time_scale``: wall-time compression factor for acquisitions; set
      to 1 to acquire in real time (e.g. to benchmark the frame rates).

    ROI and exposure are applied when a scan is prepared (staged), so a
    change mid-scan takes effect on the next scan -- the same gotcha as the
    real IOC's stream-mode file writer.

        self,
        path_provider: PathProvider,
        pattern_generator: MovingBlobPatternGenerator,
        time_scale: float = 1.0,

        self.frame_rate, self._set_frame_rate = soft_signal_r_and_setter(
            float, VENDOR_RATE_HZ[SENSOR_PIXELS], units="Hz"
        )
        self.sim_time_scale = soft_signal_rw(float, time_scale)
        self._source = AxisFrameSource(self, pattern_generator, rng=rng)

            AxisTriggerLogic(self._source),

class MovingBlobPatternGenerator(PatternGenerator):
    """A `PatternGenerator` whose blob *position* follows the wired motors.

    The upstream generator writes a fixed, centered Gaussian and only varies
    its intensity with x/y. Here the blob center also moves across the frame
    (via `set_x_frac`/`set_y_frac` in normalized [-1, 1] detector coords), so
    scans over the wired motors visibly steer the blob on the images.
    Intensity keeps the upstream pattern, and the point detector channels are
    unchanged.
    """

    def __init__(self, sleep=asyncio.sleep) -> None:
        super().__init__(sleep)
        self._x_frac = 0.0
        self._y_frac = 0.0
        self._illumination = 1.0

    def set_x_frac(self, frac: float) -> None:
        self._x_frac = min(max(frac, -1.0), 1.0)

    def set_y_frac(self, frac: float) -> None:
        self._y_frac = min(max(frac, -1.0), 1.0)

    def set_illumination(self, frac: float) -> None:
        """Scale the pattern intensity: 1 = full beam, 0 = dark (see
        `wire_illumination` for what feeds this)."""
        self._illumination = min(max(frac, 0.0), 1.0)

    def raw_point(self, channel: int = 1, high_energy: bool = False) -> float:
        """The upstream pattern value, ungated by illumination."""
        return super().generate_point(channel, high_energy)

    def generate_point(self, channel: int = 1, high_energy: bool = False) -> float:
        # Gated by illumination so a closed shutter or dumped beam zeroes
        # the pattern intensity (feeds the frame brightness in
        # `write_images_to_file` and `SimAxisSXR40`'s frame source).
        return self.raw_point(channel, high_energy) * self._illumination

    def _blob_at_position(self, height: int, width: int) -> np.ndarray:
        xs, ys = np.meshgrid(
            np.linspace(-1, 1, width), np.linspace(-1, 1, height)
        )
        cx = _BLOB_TRAVEL * self._x_frac
        cy = _BLOB_TRAVEL * self._y_frac
        d2 = (xs - cx) ** 2 + (ys - cy) ** 2
        blob = np.exp(-d2 / (2 * _BLOB_SIGMA**2))
        return blob * np.iinfo(np.uint8).max

    async def write_images_to_file(self) -> None:
        # Same acquisition loop as upstream, but the blob is regenerated at
        # the current (x_frac, y_frac) before each frame is written.
        file = self._get_file()
        start = time.monotonic()
        for i in range(1, self._number_of_frames + 1):
            deadline = start + i * self._period
            await self.sleep(deadline - time.monotonic())
            height, width = file.blob.shape
            file.blob = self._blob_at_position(height, width)
            intensity = self.generate_point() * self._exposure
            file.write_image_to_file(intensity)
            self._update_images_written(file.image_counter)

class LVMotorMoveLogic(SimMotorMoveLogic):
    """Move logic with software limits, time scaling and fault injection."""

    low_limit: float = float("-inf")
    high_limit: float = float("inf")
    time_scale: float = 1.0
    fail_next: SignalRW[bool] | None = None
    label: str = ""
    units: str = ""
    precision: int | None = None

    async def check_move(self, new_position: float) -> None:
        if not (self.low_limit <= new_position <= self.high_limit):
            raise MotorLimitError(
                f"{self.label}: requested position {new_position} {self.units} is "
                f"outside the software limits "
                f"[{self.low_limit}, {self.high_limit}] {self.units}"
            )

    async def get_units_precision(self) -> tuple[str | None, int | None]:
        return self.units or None, self.precision

    async def _simulate_move(self, new_position: float) -> None:
        """Time-based motion at the configured velocity, updated at 10 Hz."""
        velocity = abs(await self.velocity.get_value()) * self.time_scale
        acceleration_time = (
            abs(await self.acceleration_time.get_value()) / self.time_scale
        )
        old_position = await self.readback.get_value()
        await self.setpoint.set(new_position)
        distance = abs(new_position - old_position)
        if distance == 0:
            return
        if velocity == 0 or math.isinf(velocity):
            self.readback_set(new_position)
            return
        # Constant-velocity profile plus one acceleration_time of ramp padding,
        # so move_time is always >= distance / velocity.
        move_time = distance / velocity + acceleration_time
        start = time.monotonic()
        while True:
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
            if elapsed >= move_time:
                break
            fraction = elapsed / move_time
            self.readback_set(old_position + fraction * (new_position - old_position))
            await asyncio.sleep(min(0.1, move_time - elapsed))
        self.readback_set(new_position)

    async def move(self, new_position: float, timeout) -> None:
        if self.fail_next is not None and await self.fail_next.get_value():
            await self.fail_next.set(False)
            old_position = await self.readback.get_value()
            stall_position = old_position + 0.4 * (new_position - old_position)
            await self._simulate_move(stall_position)
            raise SimulatedMotorFailure(
                f"{self.label}: simulated motor failure (sim_fail_next was set); "
                f"stalled at {stall_position:.6g} {self.units} "
                f"while moving to {new_position:.6g} {self.units}"
            )
        await self._simulate_move(new_position)

class SimLVMotor(SimMotor):
    """A `SimMotor` configured from a LabVIEW motor config.

    Adds software-limit enforcement (moves and fly-scan prepare), units and
    display precision from the config, velocity/acceleration from the driver
    section, and a one-shot ``sim_fail_next`` fault-injection control.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: MotorConfig,
        time_scale: float = 1.0,
        name: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self._time_scale = time_scale
        # Sim-only control: when True, the next move fails partway then resets
        self.sim_fail_next = soft_signal_rw(bool, False)
        self.deadband = soft_signal_rw(float, config.deadband, units=config.units)
        self.add_readables([self.deadband], Format.CONFIG_SIGNAL)
        super().__init__(
            name=name,
            instant=False,
            initial_value=config.initial_position,
            units=config.units,
        )
        # SimMotor leaves the readback at 0; start it at the (clamped) setpoint
        self._user_readback_set(config.initial_position)
        self._config_values_applied = False

    async def connect(
        self,
        mock: bool = False,
        timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
        force_reconnect: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        await super().connect(
            mock=mock, timeout=timeout, force_reconnect=force_reconnect
        )
        # SimMotor hard-codes velocity=1.0 and acceleration_time=0.5 at signal
        # creation; apply the configured values once the signals are connected.
        if not self._config_values_applied:
            await self.velocity.set(self.config.velocity)
            await self.acceleration_time.set(self.config.acceleration_time)
            self._config_values_applied = True

    async def set_initial_position(self, position: float) -> None:
        """Jump to ``position`` with no simulated motion (sim-config
        ``initial_state``).

        Limit-checked exactly like a real move (raises `MotorLimitError`).
        Motor-to-AI channels linked to this motor follow via their readback
        subscription, so the whole derivation chain starts consistent.
        """
        await self.movable_logic.check_move(position)
        await self.user_setpoint.set(position)
        self._user_readback_set(position)

    @cached_property
    def movable_logic(self) -> LVMotorMoveLogic:
        return LVMotorMoveLogic(
            readback=self.user_readback,
            readback_set=self._user_readback_set,
            setpoint=self.user_setpoint,
            velocity=self.velocity,
            acceleration_time=self.acceleration_time,
            low_limit=self.config.low_limit,
            high_limit=self.config.high_limit,
            time_scale=self._time_scale,
            fail_next=self.sim_fail_next,
            label=self.config.label,
            units=self.config.units,
            precision=self.config.precision,
        )

    async def describe(self):
        descriptor = await super().describe()
        datakey = descriptor[self.user_readback.name]
        if self.config.precision is not None:
            datakey["precision"] = self.config.precision

def load_sim_devices(
    config_dir: Path | str = "lv-config",
    only_used: bool = False,
    time_scale: float = 1.0,
    seed: int | None = None,
    update_period: float = DEFAULT_UPDATE_PERIOD,
    data_dir: Path | str | None = None,
    sim_config: Path | str | SimConfig | None = None,
) -> SimDevices:
    """Parse the LabVIEW configs and return connected simulated devices.

    :param config_dir: directory containing the LabVIEW JSON config files
    :param only_used: if True, only create devices whose "... Used?" flag is
        set; default creates all devices
    :param time_scale: >1 uniformly speeds up motor motion and beam dynamics
        (config signals still report the real configured values)
    :param seed: seeds all noise/drift RNGs for reproducible values
    :param update_period: AI background update period in seconds
    :param data_dir: where the blob detector writes HDF5 files (default: a
        fresh temporary directory)
    :param sim_config: path to the static ``sim-config.yaml`` (facility
        values, sim wiring, initial state — see ``sim_ophyd._sim_config``),
        or an already-parsed `SimConfig`. Default: auto-discover
        ``sim-config.yaml`` in the working directory, else built-in defaults.

    Devices are created and connected in the bluesky event loop, so create
    the RunEngine first::

        RE = RunEngine()
        devices = load_sim_devices()
    """
    from bluesky.run_engine import (
        call_in_bluesky_event_loop,
        in_bluesky_event_loop,
    )

    # A foreign running loop (e.g. a Jupyter kernel's) is fine: the devices
    # are created in the bluesky loop, which runs in its own thread. Only a
    # call from *inside* the bluesky loop must use the async variant.
    if in_bluesky_event_loop():
        raise RuntimeError(
            "load_sim_devices() was called from inside the bluesky event "
            "loop; use `await aload_sim_devices(...)` instead"
        )

    try:
        return call_in_bluesky_event_loop(
            _build_devices(
                config_dir, only_used, time_scale, seed, update_period,
                data_dir, sim_config,
            )
        )
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Could not connect the simulated devices: the bluesky event loop "
            "is not running. ophyd-async devices must live in the same asyncio "
            "loop as the RunEngine, so create the RunEngine first "
            "(RE = RunEngine()) and then call load_sim_devices(), or use "
            "`uv run sim-beamline` which wires this up for you. In a plain "
            "asyncio program without a RunEngine, use "
            "`await aload_sim_devices(...)` instead."
        ) from exc

def labview_replay_scan(
    scan,
    *,
    start_frame=1,
    max_frames=None,
    roi=None,
    replay_timing=False,
    time_scale=1.0,
    md=None,
):
    """Replay a recorded LabVIEW scan, frame for frame.

    Emits the recorded values verbatim: the analog channels, energies and
    shutter state from the ``-AI.txt`` row, the exposure and the 93-motor
    controls snapshot from the FITS header, and the real pixels. All of it
    comes from the replay bundle plus the HDF5 frame file -- **the raw LabVIEW
    export is not needed and is never read**.

    Nothing is written. Frame selection and cropping become a ``slice`` on the
    StreamResource, so a partial or cropped replay still copies no pixels.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scan : str
        Recorded scan name, e.g. ``"TBlock6_89858"``. ``list_replay_scans()``
        shows what the bundle holds.
    start_frame : int
        1-based frame number to start from, matching the ``Frame #`` column.
    max_frames : int, optional
        How many frames to replay from ``start_frame``. Default *None* replays
        to the end of the scan.
    roi : (int, int, int, int), optional
        ``(left, top, right, bottom)`` in source pixels. Default *None* keeps
        whole frames. Frame size is per scan and recorded in the bundle.
    replay_timing : bool
        Sleep the recorded gaps between frames, so the replay takes as long as
        the original acquisition.
    time_scale : float
        Multiplier on those sleeps.
    """
    recording = ScanBundle(scan)
    frames = recording.frames(start_frame, max_frames)
    recording.check_frame_file()

    replay_ccd.configure_replay(recording.entry, first_row=frames[0] - 1,
                                n_rows=len(frames), roi=roi)
    channels = ReplayChannels(recording.columns)
    header_channels = FitsHeaderChannels(recording.header_keys)
    detectors = [replay_ccd, channels]

    ny, nx = replay_ccd.frame_shape
    source_shape = recording.shape

    _md = {
        "plan_name": "labview_replay_scan",
        "plan_args": {
            "scan": scan,
            "start_frame": start_frame,
            "max_frames": max_frames,
            "roi": list(roi) if roi else None,
        },
        "detectors": [d.name for d in detectors],
        "motors": [],
        "num_points": len(frames),
        "hints": {"dimensions": [([ENERGY_KEY], "primary")]},
        "replay": {
            "is_replay": True,
            "source_scan": scan,
            "source_frames": [frames[0], frames[-1]],
            "frames_available": len(recording),
            "roi": list(replay_ccd._roi),
            "frame_file": str(recording.path),
            "bundle": str(bundle_path()),
            "source_frame_shape": list(source_shape),
            "emitted_frame_shape": [ny, nx],
            "cropped": (ny, nx) != tuple(source_shape),
            "fits_header_channels": len(header_channels._signals),
        },
        "labview": dict(recording.meta),
    }

def labview_replay_single_snapshot():
    """Replay exactly one recorded frame. Takes no arguments.

    A convenience wrapper around :func:`labview_replay_scan` for development
    and smoke testing -- queue it as ``{"name":
    "labview_replay_single_snapshot"}`` and you get one real frame through the
    full document path without having to remember a scan name.

    It picks a small-frame scan from the middle of its illuminated range, so
    the frame has actual signal in it rather than being one of the darks, and
    crops to LabVIEW's acquisition ROI if the scan writes full 4096 x 4096
    frames. Which frame it chose is recorded in
    ``start["replay"]``/``start["plan_args"]``, so a run is always traceable.

    Needs ``LABVIEW_DATA_ROOT`` set, like every replay.
    """
    scan, frame, roi = _pick_snapshot()
    return (yield from labview_replay_scan(
        scan,
        start_frame=frame,
        max_frames=1,
        roi=roi,
        md={"snapshot": True,
            "snapshot_note": "zero-argument dev snapshot; scan and frame chosen "
                             "automatically, see plan_args"},
    ))

def labview_ccd_only_scan(
    n_frames=1,
    exposure=1.0,
    *,
    sample_name="sample1",
    sample_id="KM3245432",
    scan_prefix="lq_PS300",
    delay_between_images=0.0,
    simulate_timing=False,
    time_scale=1.0,
    image_shape=None,
    md=None,
):
    """Reproduce ``Scan Type: CCD Only, no motor movement``.

    This is what ``lq_PS300_89890`` / ``hq_PS300_89891`` are: a fixed-energy
    exposure series with no ``Beamline Energy`` column in the ``-AI.txt``.
    """
    if image_shape is not None:
        ccd.image_shape = tuple(image_shape)
    endstation.set_simulate_timing(False)
    detectors = [ccd, ai]

    _md = {
        "plan_name": "labview_ccd_only_scan",
        "plan_args": {"n_frames": n_frames, "exposure": exposure},
        "detectors": [d.name for d in detectors],
        "motors": [],
        "num_points": n_frames,
        "labview": {
            "sample_string": f"{{1={sample_name},2={sample_id}}}",
            "detector_group": "Axis Photonique",
            "scan_type": "CCD Only, no motor movement",
            "delay_between_images_s": delay_between_images,
            "curvature": 0.0,
            "clip_to_roi": "No",
            "roi": [int(ccd.roi_left.get()), int(ccd.roi_top.get()),
                    int(ccd.roi_right.get()), int(ccd.roi_bottom.get())],
            "background_roi": None,
            "scan_prefix": scan_prefix,
        },
        "sample_name": sample_name,
        "sample_id": sample_id,
    }
    _md.update(md or {})

    @bpp.baseline_decorator(endstation.baseline())
    @bpp.stage_decorator(detectors)
    @bpp.run_decorator(md=_md)
    def _inner():
        yield from bps.mv(ccd.exposure_time, exposure)
        yield from bps.mv(ccd.shutter_inhibit, 0.0)
        for _ in range(n_frames):
            if simulate_timing:
                yield from bps.sleep(
                    (exposure + CCD_OVERHEAD_SLOW + delay_between_images) * time_scale
                )
            yield from bps.trigger_and_read(detectors + [energy], name="primary")

    return (yield from _inner())

def labview_scan_series(
    spots,
    regions="CEdge_Grid",
    *,
    sample_name="sample1",
    sample_id="KM3245432",
    dark_frames=True,
    simulate_timing=False,
    time_scale=1.0,
    image_shape=None,
    md=None,
):
    """Run one ``labview_energy_scan`` per sample spot, as a series of runs.

    ``spots`` is a list of dicts of :func:`labview_energy_scan` keyword
    arguments -- typically ``scan_prefix`` plus the motor positions -- e.g. the
    2026-07-02 grid map::

        [{"scan_prefix": "Grid_0_2deg", "sample_x": 23.36, "sample_theta": 2.12, "ccd_theta": 2.45},
         {"scan_prefix": "Grid_1_2deg", "sample_x": 20.36, "sample_theta": 2.12, "ccd_theta": 2.45}]

    Each entry becomes its own bluesky run (its own Tiled node), which is how
    LabVIEW files them: one ``CCD Scan #####`` per spot. Values in a spot dict
    override the shared settings passed here.

    The signature is deliberately explicit rather than ``**kwargs``: a
    ``VAR_KEYWORD`` parameter has no default, so a form generator following the
    usual "no default means required" rule renders it as a required field.
    """
    shared = {
        "dark_frames": dark_frames,
        "simulate_timing": simulate_timing,
        "time_scale": time_scale,
        "image_shape": image_shape,
    }
    for i, spot in enumerate(spots):
        opts = dict(shared)
        opts.update(spot)
        spot_md = dict(md or {})
        spot_md.update(opts.pop("md", None) or {})
        spot_md.setdefault("series_index", i)
        spot_md.setdefault("series_length", len(spots))
        yield from labview_energy_scan(
            regions,
            sample_name=sample_name,
            sample_id=sample_id,
            md=spot_md,
            **opts,
        )

class SimCCD(Device):
    """A soft area detector that writes real HDF5 and emits StreamResource /
    StreamDatum, i.e. exactly what ``bluesky.callbacks.tiled_writer.TiledWriter``
    expects from a file-writing detector.

    One HDF5 file per run, dataset ``/entry/data/data`` with shape
    ``(n_frames, *image_shape)`` and dtype ``int16`` -- matching the
    ``Images`` extension of the LabVIEW FITS files (4096 x 4096 int16).

    ``exposure_time`` and ``shutter_inhibit`` are plain soft signals so the
    plan can drive them per point, exactly like the LabVIEW region table does.
    """

    # Per-frame in LabVIEW (FITS ``EXPOSURE`` keyword and the
    # ``CCD Camera Shutter Inhibit`` column of the -AI.txt), so these are
    # normal readings, not configuration.
    exposure_time = Cpt(Signal, value=1.0, kind="normal")
    shutter_inhibit = Cpt(Signal, value=0.0, kind="normal")
    roi_left = Cpt(Signal, value=1309, kind="config")
    roi_top = Cpt(Signal, value=526, kind="config")
    roi_right = Cpt(Signal, value=2539, kind="config")
    roi_bottom = Cpt(Signal, value=1627, kind="config")
    bin_x = Cpt(Signal, value=2, kind="config")
    bin_y = Cpt(Signal, value=2, kind="config")
    temperature = Cpt(Signal, value=-18.95, kind="config")

    #: derived scalar, the LabVIEW "Counts" column (sum over the ROI)
    counts = Cpt(Signal, value=0.0, kind="hinted")

    def __init__(self, prefix="", *, name, write_path, energy_source,
                 image_shape=(1024, 1024), **kwargs):
        super().__init__(prefix, name=name, **kwargs)
        self.write_path = Path(write_path)
        self._energy_source = energy_source
        self.image_shape = tuple(image_shape)
        self.simulate_timing = False
        self._rng = np.random.default_rng(89855)

        self._file = None
        self._dset = None
        self._path = None
        self._index = 0
        self._asset_docs = []
        self._compose_datum = None
        self._data_key = f"{name}_image"

    # -- staging ---------------------------------------------------------
    def stage(self):
        self.write_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._index = 0
        self._asset_docs = []
        fname = f"{self.name}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}.h5"
        self._path = self.write_path / fname
        # TiledWriter registers HDF5 stream assets with ``swmr=True``, so the
        # file is written SWMR-capable to match: ``libver="latest"``, all
        # datasets created up front, then ``swmr_mode = True``; after that
        # only resize-and-append is allowed, which is exactly what we do.
        # This also matches how the beamline's own sim detector writes.
        self._file = h5py.File(self._path, "w", libver="latest")
        self._dset = self._file.create_dataset(
            "/entry/data/data",
            shape=(0, *self.image_shape),
            maxshape=(None, *self.image_shape),
            chunks=(1, *self.image_shape),
            dtype="int16",
        )
        self._file.swmr_mode = True
        bundle = compose_stream_resource(
            mimetype="application/x-hdf5",
            uri=f"file://localhost{self._path.absolute().as_posix()}",
            data_key=self._data_key,
            parameters={
                "dataset": "/entry/data/data",
                "chunk_shape": (1, *self.image_shape),
                # Each StreamDatum contributes ONE new frame along a new
                # leading axis.  The consolidator defaults to "concat", which
                # would compute a dataset shape of (n_frames * ny, nx); we
                # must say "stack" to get (n_frames, ny, nx).
                "join_method": "stack",
            },

class Endstation:
    """Container that owns everything and wires the cross-references."""

    def __init__(self, write_path=None, image_shape=(1024, 1024)):
        write_path = write_path or os.environ.get(
            "BLUESKY_SIM_WRITE_PATH", "/tmp/bluesky_sim_data"
        )

        self.energy = BeamlineMotor(
            name="Beamline_Energy", units="eV", slew=MONO_SLEW_EV_PER_S, precision=6
        )
        self.energy.set(270.0).wait()

        self.mono_energy = self.energy   # BCS exposes both names

        self.motors = BeamlineMotors()

        self.ccd = SimCCD(
            name="Axis_Photonique",
            write_path=write_path,
            energy_source=self.energy,
            image_shape=image_shape,
        )

        self.ai = BeamlineAnalogInputs(
            energy_source=self.energy,
            shutter_source=self.ccd.shutter_inhibit,
            name="ai",
        )

    # -- convenience ------------------------------------------------------
    def baseline(self):
        """Devices read once at open and once at close -- the bluesky
        equivalent of the FITS primary-header motor block.

        The CCD is deliberately excluded: its image is an external stream
        asset and would force a spurious frame into the baseline stream.  Its
        ROI/binning/temperature are ``kind="config"`` and so land in the
        primary descriptor's ``configuration`` block instead, which is where
        the FITS ``ROI_*`` / ``Camera ROI *`` keywords belong.
